newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Fate of Brazil's Banerj in Cenbank hands.
newsitem.headline: Fate of Brazil's Banerj in Cenbank hands.

text.p: The fate of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj is in the hands of Brazil's Central Bank, which has to decide whether or not it will extend its administration of the bank.

"We are trying to discuss with the Central Bank what will happen (with the bank)," said Paulo Ferraz, president of private bank Bozano, Simonsen, which has been managing Banerj on behalf of the Central Bank since early January.
Banerj was due to be auctioned off today, but the state government suspended the sale after a judge ordered the re-evaluation of the bank's assets.

This was the second time the auction was suspended. The bank had been first due to be sold off on December 17, but a court injunction granted to an association of the bank's employees blocked the sale.

The Central Bank has been authorized to extend for 180 days the management of state banks Banerj and Banespa, but it has not decided yet whether or not it will keep administering the banks or not. The Central Bank's management of Banerj will expire on Friday.
The extension would give Rio de Janeiro state government more time to sell the bank and prevent it from being liquidated or turned into a federal bank.

Ferraz also said Bozano and the state government were taking measures to have the judge's order on the re-evaluation of Banerj's assets lifted, but the action turned to be less important since the Central Bank's management of Banerj expires tomorrow.
Despite all the troubles surrounding Banerj's privatization, Brazilian private bank Bradesco, one of the two bidders qualified for the auction, said it was still interested in Banerj.
The other bidder Banco Itau said it would not comment on Banerj's selloff before the auction takes place, according to a bank spokesman.
Banerj was due to be the first Brazilian state bank to be privatized.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 5074151))
